title: Recognition Scheme
description: One Destination's published rules for reading an IB Diploma in its own vocabulary: the authority that publishes them, the subject scale and grade scale they are written on, and the tables that translate an IB subject and an IB grade into them. A Destination that publishes its entry requirements in IB terms needs no record here at all — that is the default and it costs nothing. Records live in data/recognition/<destination>.json.

destination.description: The Destination whose admissions authority publishes this scheme.

name.description: The publication's own name, e.g. 'Eksamenshåndbogen — International Baccalaureate'.

label.description: How to refer to this scheme in a sentence shown to a student, e.g. "the Danish Agency's IB handbook". The engine has no words of its own for any country, so every explanation that names a translation names it from here.

display.description: How a page shows a requirement written in this scheme's vocabulary, beside its IB translation. The IB terms lead; the requirement as published follows, small, so a student can match it with the institution's own page.

requirementLabel.description: What the requirement as published is called on a page, e.g. "Danish requirement".

localOnlyNoun.description: What a card calls an option that exists only in this scheme's school system and has no IB route, e.g. "Danish-school subject" ("+ 2 Danish-school subjects").

explainedAt.description: The site path that explains how this scheme's levels read in IB terms.

averageExplainedAt.description: The site path that shows how an IB total converts to this scheme's grade average, linked from a cut-off shown in IB points.

where.description: Free note recording why the record is filed where it is. Prose, not data.

authority.description: Who publishes the rules. A translation with no publisher is our inference, not a rule.

subjectScale.description: The scale a requirement's `level` is measured on. Its id is what an Opportunity's requirement names in `levelScale`.

levels.description: Every level the scale defines, with a rank so a higher level can cover a lower requirement. Nothing outside this list is a valid `level` for a requirement on this scale.

gradeScale.description: The scale a requirement's `minGrade` is measured on. Its id is what a requirement names in `gradeScale`.

grades.description: Every grade on the scale and how it is written, so a page prints a minimum the way the institution does ("02", not "2"). Optional: without it a grade is printed as its number.

gradeConversion.description: IB numbers into this scheme's numbers. `local` is deliberately not named after the country: the engine reads this field and must not learn any country's vocabulary.

noEquivalenceNote.description: What to say when this scheme simply lists no equivalent for an IB subject and has published no specific reason.

subjectEquivalence.description: What each IB subject counts as on this scheme's subject scale. Keyed by the IB subject's id in data/ib-subjects.json. An entry with an empty `maps` records that the authority publishes no equivalent — that is a fact about the source, not a gap in our research, and `unmapped` says so.

note.description: Shown to a student alongside the translation, because a translation they cannot see the reasoning for is a claim.

unmapped.description: Why no equivalent is published. Required in spirit wherever `maps` is empty — never guess one.

subjectsWithoutEquivalence.description: Subjects a programme can require on this scale that no IB subject translates into. Without these the engine would report 'you do not have it', which reads as a rejection when the truth is that nobody has published an answer.

subjectAliases.description: Where the authority groups several of its own school subjects under one requirement heading.

subject.description: A subject name on this scheme's own scale.

level.description: A level code the subject scale defines.
